The trip ran 30.0 km against a 24.4 km optimal route, and the billed excess is 5.54 km over the 1 km tolerance, so the case is in scope for RD-1 / RD-2 [F1][F4][RD-1]. The whole deviation sits in one off-route segment, 18:44–18:55, which drove 7.35 km where the optimal route covers 2.38 km, adding 4.97 km [F3].

Consent and its scope turn on the words before the segment. At 18:41 the driver asked "Traffic ahead on Ayer Rajah Expressway is building up, shall I take another way?" [F7], and at 18:42 — before the 18:44 segment start — the rider replied "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" [F8], an acknowledgement of a general route choice under RD-5 [F8][RD-5]. The words name no road (the only road named, the Ayer Rajah Expressway, was the one to be avoided), so the named-road branch does not arise; the driver's later statement that the rider said any faster way was fine adds nothing, because a driver's statement is not consent [F10][RD-5].

The only remaining question is whether that general consent reaches this segment. A general route choice covers the route chosen to get there; it stops covering a stop away from the route or a loop of the driver's own that reaches nothing. On this record the segment is a continuous drive toward the destination — Clementi West Street 1, West Coast Road, Clementi Road, Kent Ridge Crescent and Drive, Arts Link, Computing Drive, Heng Mui Keng Terrace, Pasir Panjang Road, South Buona Vista Road — every road lying on the western corridor between Jurong Point and Suntec City [F3]. The evidence is complete — the segment's times and roads are recorded, and every chat message is timestamped — so nothing needs escalation under TH-4 [F3][F9][TH-4].
